The misfire only became visible once an error routinely named its own workflow, i.e. a new rule surfaced a latent bug in how every rule's message is decorated. When adding a document kind to scriptContext, check every method that enumerates kinds, not just the collector.

symptom: On the **legacy** engine (MXCLI_ENGINE=legacy), `create or modify workflow` that does not restate stored event handlers / boundary events / nested Ends / AI agent tasks / completion rules is written ("Created workflow") and deletes them, while the default modelsdk engine refuses the same statement with the guard-don't-drop list
cause: The workflow rewrite guards walk `ctx.Backend.GetRawUnit` with type switches on `map[string]any` / `[]any`. The legacy backend decodes with mongo-driver v1 `bson.Unmarshal` into map[string]any, which yields nested documents as map[string]any but ARRAYS AS `primitive.A` — a named type a `case []any` does not match. So every guard saw no list at all (measured with a probe: `OnWorkflowEvent primitive.A`, `Flow map[string]interface {}`). The modelsdk reader normalizes to plain slices (`modelsdk/mpr/reader_raw.go normalizeBSONValue`), which is why only legacy was blind
insight: A guard tested only with hand-built `[]any` fixtures proves nothing about the legacy engine: build the fixture, then `bson.Marshal` + `bson.Unmarshal` into map[string]any to get the shape legacy's GetRawUnit really returns (`legacyShaped` in validate_workflow_rewrite_legacy_test.go). Normalized in the guard, not in MprBackend.GetRawUnit, because catalog (`builder_regularexpressions.go`) asserts `bson.A` on raw units. Found only by running the e2e rewrite on BOTH engines — the modelsdk run was green. Other `[]any`-only raw walkers (REST body guard, queued-call guard) are suspects of the same class. Control: normalizer returning its input fails the legacy-shape tests

symptom: A layout created by mxcli whose placeholder is named anything but `Main` passes `mxcli check -p --references` AND `mxcli exec` ("Created layout"), then fails `mx check` with [CE0848] "No placeholder with the name 'Main' found. There should be exactly one." — and there is no DROP LAYOUT to undo it
cause: The write-time guard (`hasAnyPlaceholder`, mdl/backend/modelsdk/layout_write.go) asked only whether SOME placeholder existed, under any name. That was a faithful implementation of mxcli's own documented belief: CLAUDE.md and the layouts skill both said the name was a naming convention ("22 of 22 Atlas layouts follow it"). mxbuild validates it as a rule. Nothing between the author and the builder resolves a placeholder name, so check had no rule to apply either.
fix: Rule measured first, then written once: mdl/types/layout_placeholders.go `CheckLayoutPlaceholderNames`, applied by BOTH mdl/executor/validate_layout_placeholders.go (MDL081/MDL082, project-free pass) and the writer guard. Docs corrected in the same commit.
insight: The bug was a DOCUMENTED BELIEF, not an oversight — which is why grepping the code for a missing check would never have found it: the check that existed matched the docs exactly. When a guard looks deliberate and cites a rationale, verify the RATIONALE against the tool, not the guard against the rationale. One 10-minute measurement (create the layout, run mx check) overturned a sentence that had been carried in CLAUDE.md through several features. Measure against a layout NO PAGE USES, or you cannot tell a layout rule from a page-binding rule — here it errors unconditionally, which is what makes it checkable with no project.
controls: Five shapes on mxbuild 11.12.1: Main→0; Main+Content→0 (so extra names are fine, and a rule demanding all-Main would have been wrong); Content→CE0848; Main+Main→CE0849+CE0495; Main+Side+Side→CE0495 (so uniqueness is general, a second independent half of the rule).

symptom: `DROP LAYOUT Mod.Name` is a parse error. Layouts are the only doctype mxcli can create and alter but not delete, so a layout authored wrongly — including one mxcli itself just wrote — cannot be removed headlessly.
cause: Pure wiring gap. `DeleteLayout` existed and worked on BOTH engines and is exercised on every CREATE OR REPLACE LAYOUT (the replace half is a delete + create); only the grammar alternative, AST node, visitor branch and executor were missing.
fix: dropStatement alternative + ast.DropLayoutStmt + visitor branch + mdl/executor/cmd_layouts_drop.go, plus the stmt_summary and validate_duplicates switches. Pages still bound are named in a warning, not refused.
insight: Before designing a 'missing capability', check whether the backend already has it — here the delete was already on the write path, so the whole feature was four small wirings and the risk was near zero. The second question is what the DROP's dependency policy should be: mxcli has NO drop that refuses on dependents, and warn-not-refuse is also what makes drop-then-recreate work (pages rebind by qualified name — verified back to 0 errors). The warning is load-bearing because the consequence, CE1613, names the PAGE and never the layout that was removed.
controls: Dropping a layout one page used → 2× CE1613 naming the page; re-creating it under the same name → 0 errors. A page bound to a DIFFERENT layout must not appear in the warning, and an unused layout must produce no warning at all.

symptom: `describe workflow` → `create or modify` → `describe` differs: a call microflow authored with `comment 'Summarise'` comes back captioned with the microflow's name (`-- ACT_Summarise`)
cause: `formatCallMicroflowTask` printed the caption only as a trailing `-- caption` MDL comment, which the parser discards; re-execution then fell back to the builder's default caption (the microflow's short name)
insight: A trailing `--` comment in describe output is documentation, not data — anything round-trippable must be a grammar clause. Emit `comment '…'` only when the caption differs from the derived default, matching jump/wait (issuetracker #16), so an unauthored caption does not start appearing as authored. Only an end-to-end describe → exec → describe with an AUTHORED caption catches it; fixtures without captions pass either way

symptom: `create or modify workflow` over a workflow whose multi-user task needs 3 participants / 80 percent, or waits for all users, succeeds and the task afterwards needs all participants and does not wait — no refusal, `mx check` clean
cause: The rebuild writes `TargetUserInput: AllUserInput` and `AwaitAllUsers: false` for every multi-user task, and the guard-don't-drop check (`checkNoDroppedWorkflowConstructs`) only inspected `CompletionCriteria`; TargetUserInput and AwaitAllUsers were neither expressible nor guarded
insight: When auditing a guard, list every property the rebuild writes as a constant, not just the ones that look like 'configuration' — a constant default in the writer is exactly the set a rewrite silently resets. Found by diffing Studio Pro's saved multi-user task (ako/TestApp) key by key against mxcli's writer while adding completion rules. Once a property becomes authorable, the guard changes from 'cannot express' to 'restated?' (count stored non-defaults vs authored clauses)

symptom: `create or modify workflow` from `describe workflow` output deletes every notification activity (`Workflows$NotificationActivity`) and reports "Created workflow" — no refusal, `mx check` clean
cause: The reader had no case for NotificationActivity, so it became a GenericWorkflowActivity that describe prints as a `-- [Workflows$NotificationActivity]` comment; the rewrite guard (`checkNoDroppedWorkflowConstructs`) counted boundary events, ends and sub-processes but not this activity, so nothing noticed it was missing from the statement
insight: A `-- [Workflows$…]` comment in describe output is a guard gap until proven otherwise: whatever describe cannot state, a rewrite from that output deletes. Grep the describer's generic fallback against the guard's counters when adding either. Measured with the previous build on an 11.13 copy: one stored activity, zero after the rewrite; the ESP guard had masked it in the Studio Pro reference workflow, which also held a sub-process.

symptom: Every microflow with `notify workflow $Workflow;` written by mxcli fails the build: CE0166 "The 'Target' property is required" on the Notify workflow activity (11.10, 11.13; "'Activity'" on 11.6). `mxcli check` and `exec` passed
cause: A notify must name the element it reaches (NotifyTarget from 11.7, Activity before), and MDL had no clause for it; describe also omitted a stored target, so rewriting a Studio Pro microflow removed it
insight: The shipped statement was syntax for an action Mendix cannot build — nothing in the doctype tests or the skills exercised it, so it was never put through mx check. When a statement writes an action, check a Studio Pro-saved instance for properties the writer does not set: a required reference the grammar cannot express is a build failure waiting for the first user. The target's stored $Type depends on the element's kind, so resolve it against the workflow rather than asking the author to spell the type.

symptom: Two check-time validators (validate_import_mapping_find.go, validate_offline_paths.go) imported sdk/mpr directly — which CLAUDE.md's backend-abstraction checklist forbids for the executor. After porting them to the backend, coverage of every ported function was 0.0%: offlineProfilesIn, projectEntityFacts and the new openProjectForValidation were never executed by the suite.
cause: Both validators FAIL OPEN by design: an unreadable project returns nil and silences the rule rather than failing the check on something it could not inspect. The existing tests only exercised the pure helpers (offlinePathViolations) or passed an empty projectPath, so the reader half never ran.
fix: Added openProjectForValidation as the package's one read-only connect, and tests that exercise all three against a real fixture. Coverage 0.0% -> 72%/78%/100%.
insight: A FAIL-OPEN validator is the worst shape for an unverified port: break its reader and the rule stops firing, which looks exactly like a project the rule does not apply to. Nothing goes red. So for any fail-open code path, the test must assert the rule FIRES on a project that should trigger it — asserting it stays quiet proves nothing, since quiet is also the failure mode. Two setup details that decide whether such a test is real. (1) The fixture ships only an ONLINE navigation profile, so offlineProfilesIn returns empty on it either way; the test has to SEED an offline profile, and Mendix fixes the legal names (Responsive/Phone/Tablet + the *Offline variants) — an invented name is refused by the executor, which is how the first attempt failed. (2) Assert the control first: the stock fixture reports zero offline profiles, so a reader that invented one is caught before the positive assertion runs. Also worth noting the signature constraint that shaped the fix: ValidateProgram takes a project PATH, not a backend, because `check --references` validates a script against a project it never connects an executor to — so these open their own short-lived read-only connection rather than threading ctx.Backend through a public signature and every caller.

symptom: TestRoundtripPage_MicroflowButtonWithCurrentObject failed on main and on every branch cut from it: 'Expected Target: $currentObject parameter mapping in describe output', while the printed output plainly contained the mapping as "Target": $currentObject. Unit tests were green; only the integration suite (-tags integration) caught it.
cause: Not a describe regression at all. mdl/executor/identifier_quoting.go's mdlIdent quotes any identifier that does not LEX as a bare identifier, running the real ANTLR lexer. #476 (notify workflow ... TARGET) added `TARGET: T A R G E T;` to MDLLexer.g4, so the parameter named Target began lexing as a keyword token and DESCRIBE started quoting it. The output became MORE correct; the test's exact-substring assertion went stale.
fix: Made the assertion quoting-agnostic (accepts Target: or \"Target\":). Controlled by renaming the expected parameter to a name that is absent, which still fails — so the assertion continues to detect a genuinely dropped mapping rather than passing on anything.
insight: Adding a keyword to MDLLexer.g4 silently reformats DESCRIBE output for every existing element whose NAME matches that keyword, anywhere mdlIdent is used — the grammar change and the broken test are in different packages with no compile-time link, so nothing points from one to the other. When adding a token, grep the test tree for exact-substring assertions containing that word: here `grep -rn '"Target: '` found the single collision in seconds, where reading the #476 diff never would have. The deeper rule is that an exact-substring assertion on DESCRIBE output encodes a quoting decision the test does not care about; assert the mapping quoting-agnostically, or re-parse the output, since what a roundtrip test means to check is that the mapping survived. Note the input side did NOT break: TARGET was added to the non-reserved-keyword rule, so scripts writing `Target:` unquoted still parse — which is why check-mdl's 544 scripts stayed green and only this one output assertion moved.

symptom: check --references rejected a page that mxbuild builds at 0 errors: 'the constraint on Administration.Account names "System.UserRoles", which is neither an attribute nor an association of it'. Administration.Account extends System.User and System.UserRoles is declared from System.User, so it IS an association of it, by inheritance. Every inherited association was a false positive, and separately so was every cross-module one. Inherited ATTRIBUTES were fine throughout, which is what made it look like a narrow bug rather than a whole axis.
cause: associationTargetFrom matched the start entity against the association's two ends by exact equality and scanned only dm.Associations. Its doc comment said a specialisation deliberately returns false, 'the cost of being wrong is a false error on a working script' - sound while its only caller (resolveMemberOnEntity, typing an association retrieve) treated false as silence. The new XPath constraint checker's noteQualified then called the same helper and treated false as EVIDENCE, so the exact case the comment declined to chase became the finding. noteQualified did carry a three-valued guard, but it tested whether the BASE ENTITY was known - the wrong axis; Administration.Account is known.
fix: Replaced the boolean with assocResolution (resolved / missing / notAnEnd / unknown). The start entity is matched through its generalization chain (generalizationChain, built on findEntityByQN), and a chain that could not be walked to its root yields assocUnknown = silence. associationEndsByName also reads dm.CrossAssociations, whose far end is held by NAME not by element ID. noteQualified reports only assocMissing and assocNotAnEnd.
insight: A helper whose contract is 'false when it cannot establish the answer' is safe only while every caller treats false as silence; the moment one caller treats it as evidence, the comment promising restraint becomes the specification of a false positive. A boolean cannot carry 'no' and 'don't know' to two callers that need to tell them apart - if the codebase already has a three-valued resolver next door (memberResolution, ten lines up), reusing the two-valued sibling is the smell. Two cheap guards would have caught it: a fixture entity with a GENERALIZATION carrying an association, and one CROSS-MODULE association - a fixture of flat single-module entities cannot distinguish a correct resolver from one comparing two names. Establish the verdict with the build, not by reading: mx check on the rejected page said 0 errors, which settles it in one run.
